title: session-binding v1
description: THE BINDING RECORD (remote plan R10): the record the engine on the device that runs a session STORES for it, keyed by sessionId: the fields core/ownership.json gives to the owner node and does not mark derived - what only that machine observes - and nothing else. It is written only by that device's engine and stored on that device; the hub keeps a read-only mirror by cursor (R13). It carries no device: it lives on the device it describes, and the hub files its mirror under that device. The hub's own fields are the fleet record, schema/session-record.v1; no field is in both, and test/test-schema-session-binding.ps1 computes this field list from the ownership table and fails if the two ever differ. Values are plain and typed, and a field not set is absent. ON DISK and in its versioning it follows the fleet record's writer's rules: one file per session named by its sessionId, as <HordeHome>\store\sessions\binding\<sessionId>.json on the node (the fleet record is under ...\fleet\, so a local session's two files never share a name), a reader refuses a schemaVersion that is not 1, and a later version migrates by writing whole new records. Three more in-place v1 edits add fields here before Phase 3 step 3.8 ships the first writer, in order: engines K1 (the key), engines R1 (engine and resume) and lifecycle step 24 (binding, containment, predecessor, successor, closure); after that, every change is a v2.

sessionId.description: THE KEY, not a stored fact: the agent's own conversation id, which names this record and the session's fleet record alike (schema/session-record.v1). The agent owns it (core/ownership.json); the node only files the record under it.

projectCwd.x-horde-read: X2 cwd, then W1 firstCwd, then X1 cwd, then W1 cwd
projectCwd.description: The directory the session was launched in, which names its transcript's project folder; fixed at start and never revised (wezfleet Write-WfSessionRecord, firstCwd). Not the current cwd, which the agent owns. Owned by the node since remote plan R10: only the machine the session runs on knows the directory it was launched in, and the hub sees it through its read-only mirror of this record.

lastSeen.description: When the session last ran a tool, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z. wezfleet writes ToUniversalTime().ToString('o'); registry census 2026-09-30: 31 of 31 lastSeen values have this shape, and with retiredAt 46 of 46 stored timestamps. (firstSeen, which has it too, is not stored: the ownership table does not carry it.) Owned by the node since remote plan R10: only the machine the session runs on observes it, and a hub-written copy would freeze at its last value when the link drops.

lastTool.description: The name of the last tool the session ran (Bash, PowerShell, Read, Write in the registry). wezfleet writes an empty string for none, which translates to absent here: registry census 2026-09-30, present in 31 of 31 records - empty in 7 - and absent from none. Owned by the node since remote plan R10: only the machine the session runs on observes it, and a hub-written copy would freeze at its last value when the link drops.

spawnedAt.description: When the spawner launched the session, ISO 8601 in UTC with a Z. Roster census 2026-09-30: spawnedAt is present in all 422 entries - null in 116, this shape in the other 306. A null translates to absent, and absent is never read as fresh. Owned by the node since remote plan R10: only the machine the session runs on observes it, and a hub-written copy would freeze at its last value when the link drops.
